rule: Companion Part 61; Core L-503: an association found by search is a perspective within the totality (F-04). A search runs by default as the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer of a full navigation and a holistic response, and on request (L-429, M248); it is declared first with what would count as not found, and placed in the Comparative Perspective Layer after the seal, with its source, its date, what it says, how it stands with a named provision -- AGREES, DIFFERS or EXTENDS -- and, for an agreement, its grade: CONSTRUCTIONAL where both sides state the same mathematics, SELF-ADJACENT for one Navigator in one session, INDEPENDENT otherwise. It is COMPARATIVE, never inside THE ANSWER, never an authority over a reading, and the premise is not graded by it (L-490). This register holds the associations about the protocol's own provisions; sources on a Striker's matter stay in that reading's CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer.

entries.item: Pisano period (Wikipedia)
entries.says: pi(3) = 8 and pi(9) = 24, with two zeros in each period mod 9; the Pisano period equals the order of the Fibonacci matrix in the invertible 2x2 matrices modulo n
entries.with: Core Part 1: the census and the canonical 24-cycle; T(a, b) = (b, a + b) as a unit of order 24 on the 81 states (MATH-GATE)
entries.not: that the structure is all that exists; the premise is the ground, not a finding (F-02-P)
entries.not_found: a source giving another period for 3 or 9

entries.item: Pisano period, prime powers (Wikipedia)
entries.says: pi(p^k) divides p^(k-1) pi(p); whether equality always holds is open, and a counterexample would be a Wall-Sun-Sun prime
entries.with: Core FP-TowerPeriods (8, 24, 72, 216 for 3, 9, 27, 81): for p = 3, pi(9) differs from pi(3), so the periods triple at every scale; recomputed here to 3^7 (5832)
entries.not: the open question for other primes, which the tower of 3 does not touch
entries.not_found: a source stating equality fails for p = 3

entries.item: OEIS A001175, Pisano periods
entries.says: the table of Pisano periods, pi(9) = 24
entries.with: Core Part 1, the canonical cycle
entries.not: any reading of the positions
entries.not_found: a table giving another value for 9

entries.item: OEIS A030132, digital root of Fibonacci(n)
entries.says: the digital root of Fibonacci(n) is periodic with period 24 = A001175(9)
entries.with: the canonical cycle read with 9 for the residue 0 (Core Part 1)
entries.not: that digital roots carry meaning; the frame reads residues as coordinates
entries.query: digital root of Fibonacci numbers period
entries.not_found: a period other than 24

entries.item: M. Tegmark, The Mathematical Universe (arXiv:0704.0646)
entries.says: from an External Reality Hypothesis -- an external physical reality independent of us -- it argues to the Mathematical Universe Hypothesis, that this reality is a mathematical structure
entries.with: F-02 and F-04: both hold what exists to be a mathematical structure; Tegmark starts from an external reality, Omega42 posits no outside, and the structure is stipulated, not inferred (Companion 57.3)
entries.not: that Omega42 is a version of the MUH, or the MUH a version of Omega42
entries.not_found: no account holding what exists to be a mathematical structure

entries.item: S. Wolfram, The Concept of the Ruliad (Wolfram Institute)
entries.says: the ruliad is the result of following all possible computational rules in all possible ways
entries.with: F-02: one rule, T(a, b) = (b, a + b), at one modulus, 9; the ruliad holds every rule, Omega42 one -- the maximal totality and the minimal one
entries.not: which of the two is the larger account; they answer different questions
entries.not_found: no account of a totality of all rules

entries.item: A popular document on 'vortex math' (Scribd)
entries.says: digital roots of doubling and of Fibonacci numbers are read as symbols with powers of their own
entries.with: the documents' statement that the numbers are coordinates on a closed structure, not symbols read for meaning (not numerology); association on the structure stays HELD until computed (Companion 59.4, U59)
entries.not: anything about the document's claims, which are not examined here
entries.not_found: no popular reading of digital roots as symbols

entries.item: Catalan's Identity (ProofWiki)
entries.with: Companion 62.5, E01: Anchor x Antipode - Yin^2 = N(the state at the anchor) mod 9 on all 81 states is this identity at r = 18 for a Fibonacci-type sequence, where F(18) = 2584 = 1 mod 9 and the norm takes the place of 1
entries.not: that the identity is new; what is new is that three arms of every reading carry the norm of its state
entries.not_found: no identity of this form in the literature

entries.item: M. Sclar, Y. Choi, Y. Tsvetkov, A. Suhr, Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design (ICLR 2024)
entries.says: prompt formatting alone changes a model's measured performance by up to 76 accuracy points (LLaMA-2-13B, few-shot)
entries.with: Core Part 0.10, L4 (surface form decides the address) and the frozen output form of Part 8.0: a Navigator's output depends on the form it is given, which is why SR-CAS holds the input identical and M238 reports variance
entries.not: that the coordinate's own sensitivity to wording is the same phenomenon; the paper measures task accuracy, the protocol reads counts
entries.not_found: evidence that formatting does not change model outputs

entries.item: E. Malthouse, S. Russell, Y. Liang, T. Hills, The influence of exposure to randomness on lateral thinking in divergent, convergent, and creative search (Cognition, 2021)
entries.says: three pre-registered studies: random Wikipedia stimuli did not improve convergent or divergent thinking and often impaired fluency and creativity; a Bayesian meta-analysis supports the null; the authors suggest a stimulus may need to be task-related to help
entries.with: IN-17.5's procedural value -- a constraint neither the Striker nor the AI chose, interrupting habitual framing: an unchosen stimulus is not by that alone a help; the protocol's constraint is four directions on the question's own matter, not a random page, and whether it helps is what M267 and the personal contrast test (Companion 63.4)
entries.not: that Omega42's readings fail to help; the study tested random pages, not a structured reading
entries.not_found: no controlled test of random stimuli

entries.item: J. Collins, 'The premortem' (a chapter on its evidence)
entries.says: the academic literature on the premortem is thin; Mitchell, Russo and Pennington (1989) found that imagining an outcome as already happened raised the number of reasons given by about 30%, without assessing their quality
entries.with: IN-17.5's comparison with a pre-mortem or a devil's-advocate exercise: the comparison names a kind of procedure, and the evidence for that kind is itself thin
entries.not: that the comparison is wrong; it describes what the procedure does, not what it achieves
entries.not_found: no study of the premortem

entries.item: M. Gerlich, AI Tools in Society: Impacts on Cognitive Offloading and the Future of Critical Thinking (Societies, 2025), as reported by PsyPost
entries.says: a survey of 666 people with 50 interviews found frequent AI use strongly and negatively correlated with critical thinking, cognitive offloading playing a significant part; the design is correlational
entries.with: the jurisdiction (Core L-463, L-441; Companion 63.2): an AI arranged to inform judgment and never occupy it is built against the risk this study describes
entries.not: that Omega42 reduces cognitive offloading -- untested (M282, Test E); nor that the correlation is causal
entries.query: generative AI cognitive offloading critical thinking
entries.not_found: no study of AI use and critical thinking

entries.item: R. Catapano, Z. L. Tormala, D. D. Rucker, Perspective Taking and Self-Persuasion (Psychological Science, 2019)
entries.says: three pre-registered experiments (N = 2,734): taking the perspective of someone with an opposing view reduced openness to that view and weakened the attitude change from generating its arguments, through a clash with one's own values
entries.with: C1 and C2 (IN-17.5): a perspective forced on a person is not by that alone a widening; the four directions are offered to the Striker, not imposed, and their effect is what the contrast test measures
entries.not: that the four directions backfire; the study tested adopting another person's view
entries.not_found: no experiment on forced perspective-taking

entries.item: B. R. Anderson, J. H. Shah, M. Kreminski, Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation (Creativity and Cognition, 2024)
entries.says: within-subjects study (33 participants, 1,271 ideas): ideas made with ChatGPT were more alike across people than ideas made with the Oblique Strategies deck, though users made more ideas; ChatGPT users felt less responsible for their ideas
entries.with: C2 (IN-17.5): AI help can narrow what a group thinks while widening what each person lists; and C1: the control, a deck of unchosen constraints, kept ideas more varied across people; and C3: less felt responsibility is the risk the jurisdiction is built against (L-463)
entries.not: anything about Omega42 readings; the study tested ChatGPT and a card deck
entries.query: LLM generated ideas homogeneity creativity diversity
entries.not_found: no study of homogenization by AI help

entries.item: T. Fu, F. Barez, Same Question, Different Words: A Latent Adversarial Framework for Prompt Robustness (arXiv 2503.01345, 2025; EMNLP 2025)
entries.says: language models can lose performance when a prompt is reworded without changing its meaning; the worst rewordings are tied to drift in embedding space
entries.with: C4 (Core Part 0.10, L4; M238): surface form decides the address, and a Navigator's output depends on the wording it is given
entries.not: that the coordinate's sensitivity to wording is the same mechanism
entries.not_found: evidence that meaning-preserving rewording leaves outputs unchanged

entries.item: B. Atil and others, Non-Determinism of 'Deterministic' LLM Settings (arXiv 2408.04667, 2024; revised 2025)
entries.says: five models, eight tasks, ten runs at temperature 0 with a fixed seed: accuracy varied by up to 15% across runs, raw outputs were rarely identical, parsed answers were more stable
entries.with: C5 (SR-CAS): identical rules give identical computed values -- the coordinate, the counts, the arithmetic are recomputed by script -- but not identical text; a reading varies even under one Navigator, so agreement of readings needs a within-Navigator baseline (Companion 64.10, E07)
entries.not: that SR-CAS fails; its computed layer is deterministic
entries.query: LLM nondeterminism same prompt temperature zero
entries.not_found: outputs identical across runs at temperature 0

entries.item: M. Zheng, J. Pei, L. Logeswaran, M. Lee, D. Jurgens, Personas in System Prompts Do Not Improve Performances of Large Language Models (arXiv 2311.10054, 2023-2024)
entries.says: 162 roles, four model families, 2,410 questions: adding a persona to the system prompt did not improve performance over a control; choosing the best persona automatically did about as well as choosing at random
entries.with: C6 (M267): a framing that looks meaningful can act like a random one, which is why a coordinate's contribution needs a decoy beside it
entries.not: that the coordinate acts like a random framing; that is the question M267 answers
entries.query: placebo prompt control condition LLM evaluation
entries.not_found: no controlled test of prompt framings against a control

entries.item: Cogitate Consortium, O. Ferrante and others, Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness (Nature, 2025), as reported by the Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics
entries.says: 256 participants in seven laboratories, fMRI, MEG and intracranial EEG, every prediction pre-registered: IIT's sustained posterior synchronization was not found, GNWT's ignition at the end of a conscious experience was not confirmed; both theories were challenged
entries.with: C9 (Core L-498; Companion Part 52): CT-42 holds every idea as held and assigns empirical questions to studies; a pre-registered test that challenged both leading theories is the discipline CT-42's studies are written in
entries.not: anything about CT-42, which makes no neural prediction
entries.query: adversarial collaboration integrated information theory global neuronal workspace
entries.not_found: no pre-registered test of the leading theories

entries.item: M. Morganti, Is There a Compelling Argument for Ontic Structural Realism? (Philosophy of Science, 2011)
entries.says: the two arguments in the literature for the view that structure is all there is are found unconvincing
entries.with: C10 (F-02, F-02-P): Omega42 states its structure as a premise of a thought experiment and does not argue to it; where the argument to a structure-only world is contested, a stated premise is the route the frame takes
entries.not: that the premise is true or false; it is the ground, not a conclusion
entries.not_found: no critique of ontic structural realism

entries.item: Anthropic, Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet (2024), as summarized by Oxen.ai
entries.says: sparse autoencoders on a middle layer of Claude 3 Sonnet found up to about 34 million features, fewer than 300 active per token; clamping a feature (the Golden Gate Bridge) changed the model's outputs in specific, interpretable ways
entries.with: C11 (Stratum 2; Step 9.8): generation can be conditioned by selectively activating learned representations, the mechanistic correlate the protocol names for resonance
entries.not: that a coordinate in a prompt activates features in this way; untested
entries.query: activation steering interpretability features large language models
entries.not_found: no evidence that internal features can be identified and steered

entries.item: A. Petrov, E. La Malfa, P. Torr, A. Bibi, Language Model Tokenizers Introduce Unfairness Between Languages (NeurIPS 2023)
entries.says: the same text translated into different languages can be tokenized at lengths differing up to fifteen times
entries.with: C12 (L-501; Companion 56.1): a unit made for one language miscounts another, which is why each medium is counted by its own boundaries
entries.not: that the adaptors' layers are the right units; they are frozen choices
entries.query: tokenization disparities across languages in language models
entries.not_found: no difference in tokenized length across languages

entries.item: S. T. Piantadosi, H. Tily, E. Gibson, Word lengths are optimized for efficient communication (PNAS, 2011)
entries.says: across eleven languages, a word's average information content predicts its length better than its frequency does
entries.with: C12 (the CPDP): the counts the extraction reads -- letters and syllables per word -- are not arbitrary in a language; they carry structure of their own
entries.not: that the counts carry the meaning a reading gives them
entries.not_found: no cross-linguistic regularity of word length

entries.item: L. Favero, J. A. Pérez-Ortiz, T. Käser, N. Oliver, Enhancing Critical Thinking in Education by means of a Socratic Chatbot (ECAI 2024 workshop)
entries.says: with simulated learners, a tutor that asks questions scored higher on critical-thinking measures than one that answers and than a random control; no real students were tested
entries.with: C3 (L-463; the four closing questions of Step 15): a reading that ends in questions and leaves the judgment to the person is the design the jurisdiction holds
entries.not: an effect on real people; untested here and there (M282)
entries.query: AI asks questions instead of answers critical thinking
entries.not_found: no study of question-asking AI
